name: Three-Persona Brainstorm With Random Speaker Order (Strategy.RANDOM) — and When Round-Robin Is Better
query: For a brainstorming bot I want three personas — `creative`, `practical` and `critical` — to riff on a product idea, but not in a predictable order every time; some randomness in who speaks next gives better ideas. It must still end. Python. Also: when would I NOT want random and just use round-robin?
expected_behavior: Step 1: Consult references/agent-sdks.md §6 (the `round_robin / random` rows: a random child per turn; `allowed_transitions` constrains who may follow whom; every open-ended strategy needs `max_turns` or `termination`), references/agents.md §4 and §11 (`record()` / `replay()`), references/optimization.md F1/F3, and WebFetch the Python SDK `docs/agents/` before pinning the install.

Step 2: Three personas with unique names, `provider/model` and distinct instructions: `creative`, `practical`, `critical` (give a persona its own `max_turns` only if it carries tools — a tool-less persona compiles to one LLM call).

Step 3: `brainstorm = Agent(name="brainstorm", model="openai/gpt-4o-mini", agents=[creative, practical, critical], strategy=Strategy.RANDOM, max_turns=6, termination=TextMentionTermination("FINAL IDEAS") | MaxMessageTermination(9))`; optionally `allowed_transitions={"critical": ["creative", "practical"]}` to stop the critic from following itself.

Step 4: Explain RANDOM vs ROUND_ROBIN: RANDOM picks the next child at random each turn (within `allowed_transitions` if given) — good for diversity and breaking anchoring in brainstorms; ROUND_ROBIN is a deterministic fixed rotation — prefer it when order carries meaning (draft → review → approve), when runs must be reproducible/auditable, or when every child must get equal turns.
Step 5: Bounds (F1): `max_turns` plus an explicit `termination`; without them a RANDOM/ROUND_ROBIN conversation has no natural end.

Step 6: Lifecycle under `if __name__ == "__main__":` — `runtime.run(brainstorm, "Idea: a smart water bottle")`; `runtime.deploy(brainstorm)` in CI; `runtime.serve(brainstorm)` only if a persona has `@tool` workers (state `requiredWorkers`). Never `conductor deploy`.
Step 7: Optional workflow call: `AGENT` with `agentType: "conductor"`, `name: "brainstorm"`, `prompt`, `maxDurationSeconds`; never `agentType: "random"`.
Step 8: Testing note: speaker order is non-deterministic, so assert with `assert_agent_ran` / `expect(result).completed()` or `record()` / `replay()` rather than a fixed `assert_event_sequence`.
success_criteria: Explains when ROUND_ROBIN beats RANDOM (order carries meaning, reproducibility/audit, equal participation) and when RANDOM fits (diversity in a brainstorm)

Each persona has a unique `name` and its own instructions; any persona that carries tools also sets its own `max_turns` (tool-less personas compile to a single LLM call, so a parent bound is enough for them)
Deploys with `runtime.deploy(...)` and states whether `serve()` is needed — never `conductor deploy`
Any `AGENT` task uses `agentType: "conductor"` + `name: "brainstorm"` — never `agentType: "random"` or a framework name
Acknowledges the non-deterministic order in testing (`assert_agent_ran` / `record()` + `replay()` rather than a fixed sequence) and/or uses `allowed_transitions` to constrain the randomness
